Action Plan:
1. Acute left-sided headache with visual disturbance (probable migraine): Start over-the-counter ibuprofen with an anti-sickness medication (dose/route/frequency not documented); add a sugary, carbonated drink (e.g., Coke) as advised.
2. Arrange same-day in-person review for a full neurological examination. If symptoms improve substantially after medication before the appointment, patient may call to cancel; if symptoms worsen, do not improve, or new neurological symptoms develop before the appointment, contact the clinic for urgent review.
3. If inadequate relief with initial regimen, consider stepping up to specific migraine-relief medication (name/dose/route/frequency not documented) via pharmacy or at in-person assessment.
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: Sudden strong headache with visual changes since this morning.
- History of presenting illness:
  - Onset: This morning; began about 4 hours prior to consult; came on “kind of suddenly.”
  - Location: Left-sided.
  - Severity: ~6/10 (compared to prior kidney stone pain as 10/10).
  - Character/associated symptoms: Blurred vision with “zigzag lines,” dizziness, nausea, vomiting x2 at onset; worse with movement; difficulty tolerating screens.
  - Medications tried: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) taken ~3 hours before consult; no relief.
  - No prior headaches of this type.
  - Denies limb weakness; able to walk straight; no gait disturbance per patient.
  - Pregnancy: Patient doubts pregnancy.
- Past medical history: Kidney stones.
- Family history: Mother with migraines; family history of hypothyroidism.
- Medications: None reported.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.

Objective:
- Telehealth consultation; no vitals obtained.
- No in-person physical or neurological examination performed.
- No investigations performed today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache with visual symptoms:
   - Assessment: Migraine (first episode) per clinician assessment.
   - Investigations planned: Same-day in-person full neurological examination.
   - Treatment planned: Over-the-counter ibuprofen and an anti-sickness medication (dose/route/frequency not documented); drink a sugary, carbonated beverage (e.g., Coke). If inadequate relief, consider specific migraine-relief medication (name/dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Safety net: If symptoms worsen or do not improve with medication before the appointment, contact the clinic; if improved substantially before the appointment, may cancel.

2. Nausea and vomiting associated with headache:
   - Assessment: Nausea/vomiting associated with migraine.
   - Treatment planned: Over-the-counter anti-sickness medication (dose/route/frequency not documented); sugary, carbonated drink as above.

3. Health anxiety re serious neurological disease:
   - Assessment: Patient expressed concern about brain tumor/stroke.
   - Plan: Reassurance provided that presentation is consistent with migraine; same-day in-person neurological assessment arranged; advised to contact clinic if new neurological deficits or worsening symptoms develop.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; full neurological examination; documentation of fever, neck stiffness, photophobia, head/neck trauma, exertional/sexual onset, temporal tenderness/jaw claudication; medication names and doses for anti-sickness and migraine-specific therapy; pregnancy testing not performed.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Minor connection issues and clipped phrases; overall content understandable.
